title: Investigatio motuum, quibus laminae et virgae elasticae contremiscunt

deep.reconstruction: Context: Euler is deriving the equation for small transverse vibrations of an elastic rod lying along the x-axis, with deflection y(s,t). He has c^2 = S (the weight per unit length), b·c^4 = the bending stiffness (on the previous page b is shown to be a length), an end load E along the axis, a transverse end load F, and g as in his usual units (the fall in the first second, so accelerations carry a factor 2g). The previous page gave the moment equation E·y − F·x + (c^2/2g)∫dx∫ds y_tt = −b c^4 y_ss. It was differentiated once, with ds = dx constant, and divided by ds. On this page Euler differentiates once more. F drops out and he gets E·y_ss + (c^2/2g)·y_tt = −b c^4·y_ssss, which he rewrites in partial-derivative brackets 'more solito'. In modern form, with mass density ρA and bending stiffness EI, this is ρA·y_tt + EI·y_xxxx − N·y_xx = 0, the transverse vibration of a beam under axial force N = −E. Corollary I (§5): with no axial force, (1/2g)·y_tt = −b c^2·y_ssss, the Euler–Bernoulli beam equation. Euler admits that no general integral (unlike d'Alembert's solution for the string) has been found, so only particular solutions will be sought. Corollary II (§6): if the axial force is present, compression and tension must be treated separately. A rigid rod can carry compression only up to a limit that grows with its elasticity; a perfectly flexible one carries none. The critical load is the column-buckling problem, which he says he solved long ago (the 'columnae' papers). The next page treats tension applied by a weight over a pulley, giving the stiff-string equation y_tt/2g = h·y_ss − b c^2·y_ssss, whose sound is intermediate between a string's and a rod's.
errors: No mathematical errors. The derivation is correct under the stated assumptions: small slope (dy/ds ≈ 0, ds = dx), constant tension equal to −E, and no rotary inertia or shear.

The claim that the general integral 'could not yet be found' is historically accurate. The equation is dispersive and has no d'Alembert-type travelling-wave general solution; the separable/Fourier approach is the eventual route.

ideas.what: Fourth-order PDE for transverse vibration of an elastic rod (no axial load)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and Daniel Bernoulli, 1730s–1740s; the PDE form is due to Euler
ideas.where_published: Euler, Methodus inveniendi (1744), Additamentum I, for the frequencies; the PDE in later papers on elastic laminae, including E526 itself (exact earliest locus unsure)

ideas.what: Beam equation with axial tension or compression term E·y_ss
ideas.modern_name: Beam under axial load / stiff string equation (Rayleigh's stiff string)
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (this paper is cited by Truesdell for the tension-plus-stiffness combination); later popularised by Rayleigh
ideas.where_published: E526 (this memoir); discussed in Truesdell, Rational Mechanics of Flexible or Elastic Bodies (Opera omnia II 11/2)

ideas.what: Remark that compression is bounded by a critical load depending on stiffness, referred back to his column work
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler (1744 Additamentum; 'Sur la force des colonnes' 1757; later column papers of 1778–1780)
ideas.where_published: Methodus inveniendi (1744) Additamentum I; E238; later column papers

ideas.what: Admission that no general integral of y_tt = −k·y_xxxx is known, so the analysis turns to particular solutions
ideas.modern_name: Separation of variables / normal modes for a dispersive equation
ideas.usually_credited_to: Euler and D. Bernoulli; general theory via Fourier (1807–1822)
ideas.where_published: E526 and Euler's other vibration papers

deep.surprise_reason: This is a standard, well-documented derivation (the beam equation with axial load and the stiff-string combination), covered in Truesdell's history of E526. It contains nothing that the literature lacks.
transcription_corrections: In the first displayed equation, the scan prints the derivative with the fraction 'E ddy / ds^2' (E written in the numerator) rather than as a bracket; this is consistent with the transcription.
